page: Google Cloud Platform n1-highcpu-2 is an x86_64 architecture virtual machine belonging to the n1 server family. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 1 physical Intel Xeon core running at 2.3 GHz with hyper-threading enabled. The instance is configured with 2.0 GB of system memory, yielding 0.9 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results place this instance in the lower performance tiers. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance score is 1086.39, which is categorized in the bottom 25%, while the multi-core CPU performance score of 1408.88 falls into the bottom 10%. Memory bandwidth tests show read-only small block speeds of 80.82 GB/sec and large block write speeds of 11.3 GB/sec, both in the bottom 10%. Cryptographic and compression benchmarks also reflect entry-level performance, with a single-threaded gzip compression rate of 18.91 GB/sec and a PassMark CPU score of 1638.85.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the n1-highcpu-2 offers a low-cost entry point for workloads that require dedicated CPU allocation but have minimal memory requirements. The primary tradeoff is the highly constrained memory capacity of 2.0 GB, which limits its suitability for memory-intensive applications. This server is best suited for lightweight compute tasks, basic static web serving, simple background workers, and small-scale development or testing environments that do not demand high memory or storage throughput.
